summary.text: Ty Masterson is the Republican nominee for governor of Kansas and president of the Kansas Senate, an Andover Republican who has served in the Legislature since 2005. In 2024 he negotiated, with House Speaker Dan Hawkins and Gov. Laura Kelly, a plan to cut property and income taxes over five years, and his top issue is property-tax relief, including a cap on assessed-value growth that would require a constitutional amendment.

paragraphs.text: Masterson was born and raised in Butler County. Before entering politics he worked as a contractor and owned a homebuilding business, Masterbuilt Homes.
He left Kansas State University without finishing, and he filed for personal bankruptcy in 2010 after the business failed, an episode his opponent has criticized.
He and his wife, Marlo, have been married 30 years and have six children and seven grandchildren.
Masterson first won local office in Andover.
He served in the Kansas House from 2005 to 2009 and has been a state senator since 2009, representing District 16 in Butler County.
He became Senate president in 2021 and was re-elected in 2024 with 65 percent of the vote in his district.
Masterson announced his campaign for governor in July 2025, saying the state needed a governor who could reduce property taxes, lower crime and rein in state spending.
He cites his work in the Legislature on a $2 billion state tax reduction.
He defeated a crowded Republican primary field with an endorsement from President Trump and faces Cindy Holscher in the general election.
